  C. RESOLUTION NO. 23-14 RELATING TO COUNCIL REORGANIZATION
  TIMING AND REPEALING RESOLUTION NO. 21-50

  At its meeting of February 21, 2023, the City Council directed staff to prepare

  Ordinance No. 687 was approved at introduction by a 5-0 vote of the City
  Council at the February 21, 2023, City Council meeting. Adoption of Ordinance
  No. 687 would amend Title XV, Chapter 153 (Zoning Code) of the San Gabriel
  Municipal Code (SGMC) relating to Nonconforming Uses, Structures, and Lots.
  The Fiscal Year 2022-23 Adopted Budget includes the cost for required legal
  publication (Account No. 121-702-00-65-000) and codification (Account No.

  Gabriel, California, Approving Planning Case No. ZTA22-001, Amending Title

   XV, Chapter 153 (Zoning) relating to the Amortization Period for

  E. REVOCABLE LICENSE AGREEMENT WITH YZL INVESTMENT, LLC FOR USE
  OF PARKING SPACES AT THE MISSION DISTRICT PARK & RIDE LOT (257
  SOUTH MISSION DRIVE)

  In this proposed action, the City is acting as in its proprietary capacity as the
  owner of the Mission District Park and Ride Lot located on the westerly side of
  Mission Drive, adjacent to the former Mission 261 Restaurant. The property and
  business owner of the former Mission 261 Restaurant – YZL Investment LLC –
  together with its prospective tenant, obtained a Conditional Use Permit to open
  a new restaurant. In 2019, they approached the City to request use of the
  Mission District Park and Ride Lot to satisfy the minimum off-street parking
  requirement for a limited time. The proposed restaurant would need
  approximately 50 spaces; the total lot contains approximately 111 parking
  spaces. On July 16, 2019, the City Council approved an agreement for the joint
  use of the parking lot. The agreement expired in 2021 and a request for a
  renewal was not filed by the business owner. The City is expected to receive
  $1000-per-month License Fee from YZL Investment, LLC for the License Fee for
  as long as the restaurant is in operation.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the License Agreement.

  F. LEASE PURCHASE AGREEMENT IN THE AMOUNT OF $694,845.10 TO
  REPLACE AND UPGRADE FIRE DEPARTMENT RADIOS

  The San Gabriel Fire Department needs to replace its legacy radio system. The
  mobile and portable radios are over ten, and in instances, nearly twenty years
  old and in critical need of replacement. Replacement of the radios was
  previously deferred due to financial constraints. Staff has conducted research
  into several radio vendors and interoperability systems to determine the best
  radio communication system for the Department’s current and future needs.
  The Motorola APX8000 and APX8500 are the products determined to best meet
  the current needs and will provide for a 15-year service life. The total cost of
  the project including interest payments is $694,845.10.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 7, 2023  4
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. 23-11
  2. Approve a Motorola Solutions Equipment Lease-Purchase Agreement to
  replace and upgrade the Fire Department’s radio system in the amount of
  $694,845.10 and authorize the City Manager to execute all necessary
  documents.
  3. Waive formal bidding requirements in accordance with the San Gabriel
  Purchasing Policy and Municipal Code 34.35.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. SMALL BUSINESS ASSISTANCE GRANT PROGRAMS: GENERAL AND
  RELOCATION ASSISTANCE

  On January 17, 2023, the City Council directed staff to proceed with developing
  a third round of the Small Business Assistance Grant Program with two
  components: general assistance and relocation assistance. Eligible uses of funds
  for general business assistance are to improve business operations, which could
  include covering costs of commercial rental or business mortgage payment,
  utility bills, employee payroll, supplies, and new equipment. Eligible uses of
  funds for relocation assistance are to reimburse businesses that have moved
  locations within San Gabriel or from another City to San Gabriel. This staff report
  outlines the proposed program’s requirements, administration, and marketing
  and outreach plan. Total funds for the proposed program will not exceed
  $175,000.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that that City Council authorize the program and adopt
  Resolution No. 23-10 appropriating $175,000 of funding in the General Fund.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 7, 2023  5
   B. DISCUSSION REGARDING AN ORDINANCE  TO  ALLOW  LOCAL
  PROSECUTION OF CERTAIN MISDEMEANORS

  Over the past several years, crime has been increasing in San Gabriel and
  throughout the region. Not only has the area experienced an increase in violent
  crimes, but other less severe, quality-of-life crime has also risen. This has resulted
  in more graffiti, car break-ins, shoplifting, and other property damage. To
  address the increase in crime, the City Council has asked staff to collaborate with
  the City Attorney’s Office to investigate ways to locally prosecute crimes that are
  not being prosecuted by the Los Angeles County District Attorney’s Office. The
  City Attorney’s Office has identified several crimes that, if enforced, could
  prevent larger and more violent crimes from occurring. Staff is seeking direction
  on a proposed ordinance that will be brought back in the future for
  consideration of adoption. A quick review of the budgets of cities that prosecute
  misdemeanor crimes locally indicates that a cost of $200,000 to $400,000
  annually would likely be required for a city the size of San Gabriel to have the
  City Attorney’s office or an outside attorney locally prosecute misdemeanors.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council discuss the proposed Ordinance and
  provide staff with direction on how to proceed with local prosecution.

  C. RESOLUTION NO. 23-13 PROCLAIMING THE TERMINATION OF A LOCAL
  EMERGENCY

  The City of San Gabriel has been in a state of local emergency since March 16,
  2020, due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Following the State’s termination of the
  state-wide emergency on February 28, 2023, formal City Council action is
  requested to terminate the state of local emergency. There is no fiscal impact
  associated with rescinding the emergency order. Any reimbursements for
  COVID-19 impacts have been recovered through American Rescue Plan Act
  (ARPA) funds previously issued to the City.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 7, 2023  6

MINUTES OF MARCH 7, 2023

I  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Ding called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at 6:32
  P.M . on Tuesday, March 7, 2023, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission
  Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Council Member Menchaca.

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Eric Chan, Denise Menchaca, John Wu, Vice Mayor John
  R. Harrington, and Mayor Tony Ding .
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, City Attorney Keith

I  Lemieux, Community Services Director Rebecca Perez,
  Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark, Public Works Director/City
  Engineer Greg de Vinck, Fire Chief Steven Wallace,
  Human Resources/Risk Management Director Edward
  Macias,  Finance  Director  William  Kaholokula,
  Community Development Director Aldo Cervantes,
  Acting Police Chief Rikimaru Nakamura, and Assistant
  City Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and
  how to request meeting agendas.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER
  Hearing no objection, Mayor Ding announced that the Agenda Order was approved .

  2. PRESENTATIONS

I  A. WOMEN'S HISTORY MONTH

  Council Member Menchaca made the presentation.

  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  In relation to the discussion held at the City Council and Planning Commission Joint
  Special Meeting of March 2, 2023, on the subject of an inclusionary housing ordinance
  and density bonuses:

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 6  March 7, 2023
   •  Viki Goto, resident and Human Equity, Access and Relations (HEAR)
  Commissioner, provided comments on affordable housing and in favor of the
  adoption of an inclusionary housing ordinance.

  •  Cathie Chavez-Morris, HEAR Commissioner, provided comments on the need
  for affordable housing in San Gabriel.

  •  Jackie Borja, resident, provided comments suggesting that the City Council

I  •
  evaluate the 10% and 15% affordable housing options.

  Alejandra Benavides, resident, provided comments advocating for more
  affordable housing.

  •  Evelyn Torres -Rangel, resident, provided comments in favor of 15% of both
  rental and sale properties to low- and moderate-income households.

  •  Chasity Jennings-Nunez provided comments questioning whose interests the
  City Council and Planning Commission are looking out for.

  •  Sylvia Templar, resident, commented that rental prototypes are feasible with
  density bonuses, and requested that staff speak with developers that have built
  for-rent developments.

  •  Senya Lubisich, resident, expressed concern that the City might not do its best
  to have a representative amount of low-cost affordable housing as part of an
  inclusionary housing ordinance.

I  •  Erlinda Romo, resident, spoke in favor of including both rental and for-sale
  developments in an inclusionary housing ordinance, and requested that the
  study group look at how newer residential projects are basing their rent.

  Edith Gonzalez commented that middle schoolers are not included in this year's
  Pentathlon and requested City Council influence to include them.

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Vice Mayor
  Harrington, to approve Consent Calendar Items 4A - 4F as presented.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, MENCHACA, WU, HARRINGTON, DING
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN :  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

I  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved the following :

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of February 21, 2023.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of February 21, 2023.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING M INUTES  Page 2 of 6  Ma rch 7, 2023
   The City Council approved February 10, 2023, and February 16, 2023, Registers of
  Demands and Warrants for the payment of City expenditures.

  C. RESOLUTION NO. 23-14 RELATING TO COUNCIL REORGANIZATION TIMING
  AND REPEALING RESOLUTION NO. 21-50

  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 23-14 relating to Council reorganization
  and repealing Resolution No. 21-50.

I  D. ORDINANCE NO. 687 AMENDING CHAPTER 153 OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  MUNICIPAL CODE TO ADDRESS NONCONFORMING USES, STRUCTURES,
  AND LOTS (ZTA22-001) - SECOND READING AND ADOPTION

  E. REVOCABLE LICENSE AGREEMENT WITH YZL INVESTMENT, LLC FOR USE OF

  The City Council approved the License Agreement.

  F. LEASE PURCHASE AGREEMENT IN THE AMOUNT OF $694,845.10 TO REPLACE
  AND UPGRADE FIRE DEPARTMENT RADIOS

I  The City Council :

  1. Adopted Resolution No. 23-11 .
  2. Approved a Motorola Solutions Equipment Lease-Purchase Agreement to
  replace and upgrade the Fire Department's radio system in the amount of
  $694,845.10 and authorized the City Manager to execute all necessary

  3. Waived formal bidding requirements in accordance with the San Gabriel

  7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. SMALL BUSINESS ASSISTANCE  GRANT  PROGRAMS:  GENERAL  AND
  RELOCATION ASSISTANCE

I  Economic Development Manager Caroline Velarde made the presentation.

  Clarifying discussion included that if insufficient applications are received,
  applications would continue to be accepted; staff would return to the City Council
  for direction on surplus funds; staff would put an item on the Consent agenda to
  fund the first group of grants; outreach to businesses; qualifications for applicants;
  and if applicants previously received a grant of $2500, that amount could be
  subtracted from a subsequent $10,000 grant.

  There was no public comment.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 6  March 7, 2023
   Discussion included consideration of sales tax payment history for applicants;
  eligibility components; whether businesses which received previous grants are still
  in business; clarification that relocation is only available for businesses within the
  City; and the possibility that the proposed amount would be money better spent
  on the whole community,

  A motion was made by Mayor Ding, seconded by Council Member Wu, to authorize
  the program and adopt Resolution No. 23-10 appropriating $175,000 of funding

I  in the General Fund, as amended to reduce the grant amount to individual grantees
  by the amount of a previously-received Community Development Block Grant.

  Motion carried by a vote of 3-2 as follows:

  AYES:  MENCHACA, WU, DING
  NOES:  CHAN, HARRINGTON
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  B. DISCUSSION REGARDING AN ORDINANCE TO ALLOW LOCAL PROSECUTION
  OF CERTAIN MISDEMEANORS

  Assistant City Attorney Koczanowicz made the presentation.

  Clarifying discussion included that the City Attorney's office would be the
  prosecuting arm for the specific misdemeanors detailed in the staff report; the City
  Attorney's firm has numerous attorneys who specialize in code and criminal
  prosecution; initial budget allocation would be $150,000 and costs would only be

I  incurred if prosecution takes place; though the District Attorney (DA) is not
  prosecuting certain crimes, the San Gabriel Police Department continues to arrest
  people and doesn't assume they won't be prosecuted; reaffirmation that the five
  misdemeanors listed in staff report meet criteria, particular to the City of San
  Gabriel, for the City to prosecute those misdemeanors; cost of crime in the City;
  misdemeanor and prosecution statistics; double jeopardy definitions and
  declination to file; the Police Department's discretion on which agency to file with;
  and average cost per case to prosecute.

  The following spoke or provided comments in opposition to local prosecution: Dr.
  Chasity Jennings-Nunez; Patricia Fulton, resident; and Erlinda Romo, resident.

  Andrew, resident, commented on community-based prevention, rescission of the
  City's Memorandum of Understanding with the Department of Homeland Security,
  and the value of investment in prosecution if judges are lenient.

  Discussion included the Council 's responsibility to provide the safest environment
  it can to residents, businesses, and visitors; changes in crime categories;

I  components of diversion including discretion in consequences; seen and unseen
  costs and consequences of completed and uncompleted crimes to individuals and
  the City; various Police Department programs in effect; value of data and cost
  analysis relative to local prosecution; the City's control of the number of cases
  prosecuted; and the necessity of consequences to help the offender and the
  community.

  RECESS AND RECONVENE

  CITY COUNC IL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 4 of 6  March 7, 2023
   The meeting was recessed at 9:04 P.M. and reconvened at 9:15 P.M. with all Council
  Members present.

  Discussion continued that the proposed ordinance is insufficient to patch the hole
  left by Special Directive 20-07; all Council Members support public safety as a
  priority; calls from business owners every month on broken windows; the purpose
  is not to punish, but to prevent by having consequences; helping victims by
  prevention; precedent in Redondo Beach having done its own prosecution for 10
  years; the ordinance provides for prosecutorial discretion with a focus to deal with

I  issues through diversion; and reevaluation of local prosecution in one year.

  The City Council unanimously directed staff to prepare an ordinance for City
  Council consideration.

  C. RESOLUTION NO. 23-13 PROCLAIMING THE TERMINATION OF A LOCAL
  EMERGENCY

  City Manager Lazzaretto made the presentation.

  There was no public comment.

  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Vice Mayor
